newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle calls mixed, feeders steady to up.

text.p: Early calls on CME live cattle futures ranged from 0.100 cent lower to 0.100 higher while feeder cattle were expected to open steady to up 0.100 cent, livestock analysts said.

Analysts looked for light resistance in December as it holds a premium to cash. The boxed beef market also ranged mixed on Wednesday which may limit buying interest. Further rolling of long positions will likely support back months, they said.
Trading is expected to be light as the market awaits Friday's Cattle-on-Feed Report and looks ahead to the holidays, they said.

Estimates on the cattle report for major feedlots of 1,000 head or more averaged 103.2 percent of last year for on-feed numbers as of December 1, ranging from 102 to 104.2 percent. November placements averaged 105 percent in a range of 98 to 110 percent and marketings averaged 93.9 percent in a range of 91 to 98 percent of last year.
Feeders were expected to show some early support after corn futures eased late Wednesday. Early gains in corn futures weighed on feeders most of Wednesday, analysts said.
January and March fell through 40-day moving averages to finish down near lows Wednesday, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.02 at $65.45 per cwt.
